home.seoDescription: Explore Jalaranu's underlake datacenter project, validation approach, and partnership opportunities for computing infrastructure in Indonesia.

hero.h1: Computing infrastructure **beneath the lake**. Supporting Indonesia's ==digital resilience==.
intro: Jalaranu is developing a modular underlake datacenter project. The focus is to evaluate **thermal efficiency, operational reliability**, and the feasibility of deployment in Indonesia.
We welcome collaboration with investors, institutions, and technology partners to establish a measurable foundation for development.
hero.caption: Project illustration. Final configuration is subject to study and engineering findings.
hero.imageAlt: Project illustration: the Jalaranu datacenter module beneath the lake surface, connected to shore-based support facilities by protected power and communication routes.

slides.alt: Lake Batur, Bali, seen from its volcanic shore
Lake Matano, South Sulawesi, an ancient deep-water lake

why.h2: Why consider a location **beneath a lake**?
body: Underwater placement offers a different approach to heat management, physical space, and infrastructure access. Its potential benefits need to be assessed alongside the implications for deployment, maintenance, connectivity, and recovery.
The central question is: under what conditions would this approach be more feasible than a land-based datacenter using water-based cooling?
Jalaranu places that comparison at the centre of its evaluation.

focuses.title: Thermal performance
focuses.body: **Assessing heat transfer** and energy demand under defined site conditions and workloads.

focuses.title: Operational reliability
focuses.body: **Testing how the system can be monitored, maintained, and recovered** when disruptions occur.

focuses.title: Overall feasibility
focuses.body: **Comparing whole-life costs** and responsibilities towards the environment.

system.h2: One system, from shore to submerged module.
system.body: The Jalaranu project connects shore-based support facilities with a computing module beneath the water. Planning covers power, connectivity, heat management, monitoring, and how the module is deployed and retrieved.

items.title: Shore facilities
items.body: Interfaces for power, networking, and operational management.

items.title: Shore-to-module connections
items.body: Power and communications routes to be designed around service-continuity requirements.

items.title: Underwater module
items.body: A computing enclosure and supporting systems to be evaluated through engineering and testing.

items.title: Monitoring and recovery
items.body: Observation of system conditions, incident response, and module retrieval.

body: Each development stage needs to answer specific questions: does performance meet the requirement, how does the system behave when it fails, what does it cost to operate, and how are environmental effects assessed?
Test plans, measured results, and their limitations provide the basis for decisions about further development.
